title: DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2.5 Aims to Make Robots Safer, More Dexterous, and Faster Learners
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/deepmind-gemini-robotics-2-5/en/headerimage/tripadvisor-tca-migration-1795623375360.jpeg"/><p>Google DeepMind introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5, a vision-language-action (VLA) model designed to improve robots' dexterity, reliability, and learning speed, while enabling safer operation in unstructured real-world environments.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: GitHub Ditches CSS-in-JS for CSS Modules, Reports 55% Faster SSR After Three-Year Migration
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/github-css-migration/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795537886697.jpg"/><p>GitHub migrated github.com from styled-components to CSS Modules over three years, reporting a 55% cut in server-side rendering time and 25% faster component initialisation. Primer components were converted behind feature flags, and about 7,760 sx prop usages were migrated with codemods and Copilot agents. Commenters questioned user impact and hashed class names.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: DoorDash Scales Dispatch 10x While Maintaining 99.99% Peak Availability
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/doordash-dispatch-redesign/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793847001864.jpg"/><p>DoorDash has redesigned its real-time dispatch platform, replacing a monolithic optimization engine with a distributed architecture that separates coordination from computation. The new system delivers 10x higher throughput and more than 99.99% peak availability. It also supports hybrid machine learning inference and multi-agent reinforcement learning to dynamically optimize delivery assignments.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Vercel Launched Experimental Board to Coordinate Tasks Across Humans and Coding Agents
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/vercel-board-agents/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795183495782.jpg"/><p>Vercel's experimental Board is a headless message store where people and coding agents claim leased tasks, declare dependencies, and sync threads with Slack, GitHub, and Linear.</p> <i>By Daniel Dominguez</i>

title: Presentation: Learning Out Loud (Under Near-Existential Pressure)
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/ai-engineering-culture/en/mediumimage/LauraSavino-medium-1793278596285.jpeg"/><p>Laura Savino discusses the psychological friction of AI adoption for senior engineers & architects. She explains how shifting from static expertise to learning in public lowers anxiety, accelerates tooling fluency, and prevents burnout. Leaders will discover actionable strategies to support their teams, debunk tech zealotry, and foster an adaptive engineering culture that thrives during upheaval.</p> <i>By Laura Savino</i>

title: Rust 1.100 Ships the Never Type After Ten Years and Five Failed Attempts
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/rust-1-100-never-types/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795523502483.jpg"/><p>Rust 1.100.0, released 12 November 2026, stabilises the never type (!) after ten years of work and makes Infallible an alias for it. The release also stabilises the core of the allocator API, adds DropGuard, and gives Cargo an opt-in dependency cooldown setting. Some critics note the allocator design still lacks inline storage support.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: AWS Lambda Doubles Its Timeout to 30 Minutes After Eight Years at 15
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-lambda-30-minute-timeout/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795522224655.jpg"/><p>AWS has raised the maximum timeout of on-demand Lambda Event Functions from 15 to 30 minutes in all commercial regions, with no opt-in and no new pricing. The limit had stood since 2018. AWS's post lists the costs: twice the concurrency at the same request rate, three-hour SQS visibility timeouts, and Kafka mappings that must be recreated. Practitioners welcome it and ask what belongs elsewhere.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Automating Spark Upgrades with Codex Agents at OpenAI
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/openai-spark-fleet/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795548261270.jpg"/><p>At QCon San Francisco 2026, Mouli Mukherjee, Engineering Manager for Data Infrastructure at OpenAI, argued that AI agents are most useful not for rebuilding a data platform, but for the open-ended operational work that is hard to turn into fixed playbooks.</p> <i>By Robert Krzaczyński</i>

title: CNCF Research Shows Virtual Machines Remain Central as AI Workloads Evolve
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/cncf-vm-ai-workloads/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794993904528.jpg"/><p>New research from the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) and Linux Foundation Research finds that VMs host an average of 53% of production applications, while emerging AI and agentic workloads are creating additional demand for virtualisation, particularly where stronger execution isolation is required.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: OpenAI Scales Git for Coding Agents with Pando
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/openai-git-pando/en/headerimage/openai-pando-header-1795331180238.jpeg"/><p>OpenAI has detailed Pando, a new backend that scales Git for concurrent coding-agent workloads without replacing familiar Git workflows. The company reports nearly 80% lower median push latency by coordinating branch updates independently and reusing stored packfiles across fetches.</p> <i>By Eran Stiller</i>

title: Presentation: Inferencing for Enterprises
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/enterprise-ai-inference-architecture-costs/en/mediumimage/dio-rettori-medium-1793800900455.jpeg"/><p>Dio Rettori discusses the operational realities of enterprise AI inference. Moving beyond fast token generation, he explores why inference requires dedicated systems engineering, tackles GPU utilization pitfalls, compares on-prem versus cloud TCO, and analyzes multi-agent latency determinism. He shares why teams must embed domain ontology directly into models rather than relying solely on RAG.</p> <i>By Dio Rettori</i>

title: Article: Engineering Around Non-Determinism: Evals, Grounding, and Release Gates for AI-Drafted Suspicious Reports
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/llm-agent-architecture-evals-grounding/en/headerimage/llm-agent-architecture-evals-grounding-header-1795173682566.jpg"/><p>Moving GenAI into high-stakes production requires treating non-determinism as an engineering problem. This architectural blueprint shows engineering leaders and architects how to build trustworthy agentic workflows using knowledge graphs, dual-layer eval judges, CI/CD release gates, and regression testing against golden datasets to automate drafting while maintaining zero-hallucination compliance.</p> <i>By Ritesh Modi, Sasidhar Gudala</i>

title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Lessons from Building a $100M Product in Six Weeks at OpenAI
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/qcon-sf-openai-lessons/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1795453078651.jpg"/><p>At QCon San Francisco 2026, OpenAI's Brian Yang described building the ChatGPT ads product with Codex agents and no human-written code. He outlined layered testing, sandboxes, and batched pull request reviews, and noted failure modes such as code "slop" and unsafe agent actions. He advised gradual adoption and framed engineers as managers of agents.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Securing AI Agents in Production
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/qcon-ai-agent-security/en/headerimage/header-1795213847070.jpeg"/><p>At QCon San Francisco, Google's Amanda Walker framed AI agents as an insider-risk problem operating at machine speed, and described identity, credential and containment patterns for running them safely in production.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

title: How LinkedIn Built a View-Agnostic Analytics System for Modern iOS UI Architectures
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/linkedin-view-agnostic-analytics/en/headerimage/linkedin-view-agnostic-analytics-1795455502517.jpeg"/><p>To address the challenge posed by modern iOS UI systems where the logical UI structure may not mirror the native UIKit hierarchy, LinkedIn engineers developed a view-agnostic analytics system build around a shared MeasurableNode contract.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>
